variants.name: 01-xinye-warm-stone
variants.title: 新野 · 暖石古城
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: premium AA-quality Three Kingdoms strategy/card-game TERRAIN ENVIRONMENT REFERENCE, not a user-interface mockup.
Create ONE finished, exceptionally crisp, high-resolution landscape 16:9 environment illustration: a late-Han Chinese town's spacious, level limestone courtyard, in refined semi-realistic hand-painted 2.5D game art. Subject: warm ivory limestone pavement with convincing small-scale chisel grain, restrained worn edges, delicate contact shadows and irregular non-repeating stone sizes; the ground looks solid and sharp rather than a blurry beige diamond pattern.
Composition is absolutely critical: orthographic, steep overhead playable-map view, no horizon, no sky, no depth-of-field. At least 75% of the image, spanning the entire middle, is unobstructed continuous flat ground. It must read as a navigable card battleground, NOT a scenic painting, city diorama, arena pit, or lane. Keep all decorative objects strictly in a narrow outer 10% fringe: cropped blue-gray ceramic eaves and warm timber structures at the far perimeter, one restrained golden ginkgo canopy in an outer corner, a few low shrubs and small earthenware containers at the extreme edge. The buildings frame the scene rather than fill it. Open, straight, broad traversable pavement in the center and toward all four edges, no walls partitioning the picture.
Art direction: warm Chinese ink-and-parchment sensibility compatible with cream paper, aged gold and vermilion UI, but rendered with finely resolved physically convincing stone, timber, foliage and soft sunlight. Premium commercial AA environment concept polish, sophisticated forms and material separation, strong clean silhouettes, realistic restrained ambient occlusion, subtle surface roughness, warm neutral palette, nuanced painted shading. Central pavement is visually calm with low-frequency value variation so foreground cards will read clearly; beautiful detail is concentrated at the perimeter. Fine stone grain must remain legible at game-camera distance, not excessive gritty noise.
Avoid: ANY UI, labels, text, borders, cards, characters, troops, cursors, icons, grids, logo or watermark. No bridges, streams, ponds, moats, staircases, raised platforms, monuments, central buildings, rocks in the playable area, forced winding paths or dramatic shadows crossing the center. No blur, haze, bloom, bokeh, watercolor wash, oversharpening halos, repeated oversized tiles, fisheye or toy-like mobile-game plastic. This is a terrain-only art reference, not a screenshot.

variants.name: 02-jingchu-bamboo-slate
variants.title: 荆楚 · 青石竹庭
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: premium AA-quality Three Kingdoms strategy/card-game TERRAIN ENVIRONMENT REFERENCE, terrain only.
Create ONE finished, extraordinarily clear, high-resolution landscape 16:9 ground environment in refined semi-realistic hand-painted 2.5D game art, from a steep overhead orthographic gameplay camera. No horizon, no sky, no vanishing-point depth blur. Theme: a peaceful southern Jingchu courtyard in the late-Han era. Clean, warm-gray blue-slate paving with subtle mineral veins, fitted smaller stone slabs, restrained roughness and a few modest wear marks; convincing stone thickness only at the extreme edge, all playable ground on ONE flat plane. This must be a distinctly different city from a warm limestone market courtyard, but use the SAME sophisticated painted-material rendering family.
Composition: keep at least 75% of the entire picture as a wide, flat, empty, uninterrupted central playable ground. Decoration occupies only a narrow outer fringe: cropped mature bamboo clusters, restrained dark-timber and slate-tiled eaves near the outermost edge, soft green plants in small isolated peripheral clusters, a few carefully arranged natural stones OUTSIDE the central ground. The view should suggest a richly crafted Chinese place while leaving ample empty room for cards and mouse movement. Ground remains continuous in all four directions. No water feature, no bridge, no building dividing the map.
Material and lighting quality: premium polished AA strategy RPG environment concept, elegant composition, precise stone edges, expertly grouped foliage, believable matte timber and ceramic roof texture, delicate soft sun from upper left, controlled local contact shadows. Palette of warm gray slate, muted jade green, charcoal blue and small amber accents complements an aged cream parchment/gold/vermilion UI; the center remains light and neutral, not green or overly dark. Unobstructed pavement gets calm macro forms and crisp microdetail, never busy speckled noise. The perimeter can be painterly but never fuzzy.
Avoid: UI, text, labels, title, cards, characters, troops, cursors, ornaments floating on top, watermark. No stream, pond, moat, bridge, steps, central pavilion, long wall through the center, obelisks, obstacles, isolated raised ground, circular arena or forced corridor. No mist, bloom, depth-of-field, watercolor blur, photographic grit, moss covering the center, repeating large diamond paving, plastic mobile-game look, European or Japanese architecture. Terrain reference only, not an in-game screenshot.

variants.name: 03-luoyang-han-courtyard
variants.title: 洛阳 · 汉阙石庭
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: premium AA-quality Three Kingdoms card-strategy TERRAIN ENVIRONMENT REFERENCE, no UI.
Create ONE exceptionally polished, razor-clear high-resolution landscape 16:9 late-Han Chinese administrative courtyard, seen through a steep overhead orthographic GAMEPLAY camera. This belongs to the same refined semi-realistic hand-painted 2.5D art family as a Chinese parchment-and-vermilion strategy game, not photoreal video, not a miniature toy diorama.
The defining design is a broad EMPTY, LEVEL expanse of gently weathered warm light-gray stone paving. At least 75% of the entire canvas must be continuous, open central play area. All objects stay in a shallow outer 10% framing fringe. On that fringe only: cropped imposing Han-era gray masonry and dark blue ceramic eaves, small sections of heavy dark timber gateposts, a pair of understated bronze lantern stands far apart at the edge, sparse restrained clipped plants. These hint at Luoyang's grand civic character without constructing a building, gate arch, staircase or wall across the playable space. No monumental central motif. The road is open and navigable in every direction.
AA visual target: exceptionally resolved chisel-cut limestone and slate grains, delicate stone edge wear, superb material distinction between stone/bronze/wood/ceramic, realistic soft sunlight, subtle baked ambient occlusion restricted to object contacts, precise architectural forms, coherent scale, very high-quality painted foliage, sophisticated low-saturation ivory/stone-gray/ink-blue palette with a touch of warm bronze. Central texture must be sharp but quiet and matte: enough fine detail to avoid looking upscaled, not a noisy floor that competes with cards. Ground slab sizes and joints are natural and understated, never giant regular diamonds or a checkerboard.
Avoid completely: text, inscriptions, UI, frame, cards, characters, troops, cursor, icons, logos, watermarks, water, bridges, channels, staircases, elevation changes, central monuments, statues or buildings, road obstacles, continuous barrier across the center, circular battle arena, dark cast shadows spanning the middle. No blur, soft-focus, haze, bokeh, bloom, watercolor blotches, smeary stone, ornate fantasy palaces, golden spectacle, toy-plastic game art, or perspective horizon. Terrain concept reference only, not a screenshot.
